papers.title: MoE-Mamba: Efficient Selective State Space Models with Mixture of Experts
papers.abstract: State Space Models (SSMs) have become serious contenders in the field of sequential modeling, challenging the dominance of Transformers. At the same time, Mixture of Experts (MoE) has significantly improved Transformer-based Large Language Models, including recent state-of-the-art open models. We propose that to unlock the potential of SSMs for scaling, they should be combined with MoE. We showcase this on Mamba, a recent SSM-based model that achieves remarkable performance. Our model, MoE-Mamba, outperforms both Mamba and baseline Transformer-MoE. In particular, MoE-Mamba reaches the same performance as Mamba in $2.35\times$ fewer training steps while preserving the inference performance gains of Mamba against Transformer.

papers.title: Taipan: Efficient and Expressive State Space Language Models with Selective Attention
papers.abstract: Efficient long-context language modeling remains a significant challenge in Natural Language Processing (NLP). While Transformers dominate language tasks, they struggle with long sequences due to quadratic computational complexity in training and linearly scaling memory costs during inference. Recent State Space Models (SSMs) such as Mamba offer alternatives with constant memory usage, but they underperform in tasks requiring extensive in-context retrieval. We introduce Taipan, a novel hybrid architecture that combines Mamba-2 with Selective Attention Layers (SALs). These SALs identify tokens requiring long-range interactions, remove less important features, and then augment their representations using the attention module. This approach balances Mamba's efficiency with Transformer-like performance in memory-intensive tasks. By constraining the attention budget, Taipan extends accurate predictions to context lengths of up to 1 million tokens while preserving computational efficiency. Our experiments demonstrate Taipan's superior performance across various scales and tasks, offering a promising solution for efficient long-context language modeling.

papers.title: Efficient Unstructured Pruning of Mamba State-Space Models for Resource-Constrained Environments
papers.abstract: State-space models (SSMs), particularly the Mamba architecture, have emerged as powerful alternatives to Transformers for sequence modeling, offering linear-time complexity and competitive performance across diverse tasks. However, their large parameter counts pose significant challenges for deployment in resource-constrained environments. We propose a novel unstructured pruning framework tailored for Mamba models that achieves up to 70\% parameter reduction while retaining over 95\% of the original performance. Our approach integrates three key innovations: (1) a gradient-aware magnitude pruning technique that combines weight magnitude and gradient information to identify less critical parameters, (2) an iterative pruning schedule that gradually increases sparsity to maintain model stability, and (3) a global pruning strategy that optimizes parameter allocation across the entire model. Through extensive experiments on WikiText-103, Long Range Arena, and ETT time-series benchmarks, we demonstrate significant efficiency gains with minimal performance degradation. Our analysis of pruning effects on Mamba's components reveals critical insights into the architecture's redundancy and robustness, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained settings while broadening Mamba's applicability.

papers.title: Motif-Mamba: network motif improved mamba for long-range sequence modeling
papers.abstract: Efficient long-sequence modeling remains a central challenge for large language models, as self-attention scales quadratically with sequence length. Mamba offers a linear-time alternative through selective state space recurrence, but its predominantly diagonal state transitions restrict explicit interactions among state dimensions. We propose Motif-Mamba, a structured state space model that augments Mamba with a motif-constrained low-rank recurrent pathway. Inspired by the dynamics of three-node network motifs, the proposed pathway projects hidden states into a compact dynamical subspace, imposes motif-guided interactions, and maps the resulting dynamics back to the original state space. This design enhances cross-dimensional communication while preserving the linear-time recurrent structure of Mamba. Experiments on long-sequence extrapolation, language modeling benchmarks, and brain--computer interface decoding show consistent improvements over Mamba backbones, suggesting that motif-guided low-rank dynamics provide an effective structural prior for long-range sequence modeling.

papers.title: Harmonic: Hierarchical State Space Models for Efficient Long-Context Language Modeling
papers.abstract: We present Harmonic, a hierarchical state space model (SSM) for language modeling. The architecture stacks three recurrent levels at progressively slower timescales; each level receives the prediction error of the level below as input, rather than its raw hidden state. On enwiki8 with equal token budgets, Harmonic outperforms a comparable Transformer (28M params) by +1.4% at 1K tokens, +6.7% at 8K tokens, and +11.4% at 32K tokens (bpt, lower is better). It also outperforms Mamba at every tested length by 0.7--1.8%. At 64K tokens, both Mamba and Transformer run out of memory on an 80GB H100; Harmonic trains successfully, reaching 6.169 bpt. Results replicate on WikiText-103 (H-TF gap +1.7% to +7.2% across 1K--32K). At 1B parameter scale, replacing all attention layers in TinyLlama 1.1B with HarmonicBlock eliminates the RoPE positional encoding limit: the resulting Hallamonic model maintains stable loss across sequence lengths 1K--8K on two independent clean benchmarks (Lambada and fineweb-edu held-out), while TinyLlama degrades catastrophically past its 2K-token RoPE limit (gap: +9.4 bpt at seq=8K on Lambada). Compute is O(L) per forward pass vs. O(L^2) for attention. Logs: https://github.com/Omibranch/harmonic-logs.

papers.title: Mamba with Hierarchical Memory: Solving Representation Bottleneck in Long Sequence Modeling
papers.abstract: Recurrent linear attention models (RLAs) such as Mamba offer efficient linear-time sequence modeling as an alternative to Transformers, yet their fixed-capacity recurrent states limit long-sequence modeling. Drawing inspiration from hierarchical human memory, we propose Hierarchical Memory Mamba (HMM) to address this limitation. Building upon a pre-trained Mamba backbone, HMM integrates a lightweight working memory that extracts slow paragraph-level semantics (PLS) from the fast sensory memory embedded in the backbone's hidden states. The PLS is subsequently compressed into persistent long-term memory for task-relevant retrieval. The hierarchical processing of semantic information overcomes the representation bottleneck of RLAs and endows HMM cross-task generalization through parametric learning, which is not observed in other long-context enhanced Mamba variants. Evaluations on Passkey Retrieval and LongBench-E tasks demonstrate that HMM improves retrieval success by 34.3--37.1% and reasoning accuracy by 1.6--14.2% over strong Mamba-based models, while adding only 2% extra parameters and with minimal training overhead.

papers.title: Advancing Intelligent Sequence Modeling: Evolution, Trade-offs, and Applications of State-Space Architectures from S4 to Mamba
papers.abstract: Structured State Space Models (SSMs) have become a prominent class of sequence models, developed against two long-standing difficulties: the sequential computation and gradient propagation limits of Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), and the quadratic time and memory cost of self-attention in Transformers. By combining structured recurrence with state-space representations, SSMs attain linear or near-linear scaling in sequence length and hold a constant-size recurrent state during autoregressive decoding, so that no key-value cache grows with context. This paper is a structured review of the lineage running from the Structured State Space Sequence model (S4), through its diagonal and simplified successors S4D, Diagonal State Spaces (DSS) and S5, to the selective models Mamba and Mamba-2, and on to SSM-attention hybrids. Rather than describing models one at a time, the analysis is organized around cross-cutting design dimensions: input-dependent selectivity, the recurrent and convolutional views and when each is preferable, diagonalization, cache behavior at inference, hardware-aware kernels, and hybridization. Structured state-space duality is treated as a central thread, because it accounts for the equivalence between the recurrent and the attention-like form and for why hybrid designs work. Reported efficiency and accuracy results are presented with their measurement configuration and evidence level, because observed speedups reflect the combined effects of the algorithm, implementation kernel and hardware rather than an intrinsic property of the model alone. SSMs are competitive with Transformers and more efficient in specific long-context regimes, whereas attention retains an advantage on tasks dominated by exact retrieval and associative recall. The review closes with limitations, failure modes, deployment considerations and open problems.

papers.title: Samba: Simple Hybrid State Space Models for Efficient Unlimited Context Language Modeling
papers.abstract: Efficiently modeling sequences with infinite context length has long been a challenging problem. Previous approaches have either suffered from quadratic computational complexity or limited extrapolation ability in length generalization. In this work, we present Samba, a simple hybrid architecture that layer-wise combines Mamba, a selective State Space Model (SSM), with Sliding Window Attention (SWA). Samba selectively compresses a given sequence into recurrent hidden states while still maintaining the ability to precisely recall recent memories with the attention mechanism. We scale Samba up to 3.8B parameters with 3.2T training tokens and demonstrate that it significantly outperforms state-of-the-art models across a variety of benchmarks. Pretrained on sequences of 4K length, Samba shows improved perplexity in context lengths of up to 1M in zero-shot. When finetuned on 4K-length sequences, Samba efficiently extrapolates to a 256K context length with perfect memory recall on the Passkey Retrieval task, and exhibits superior retrieval extrapolation on the challenging Phonebook task compared to full-attention models. As a linear-time sequence model, Samba achieves a 3.73x higher throughput compared to Transformers with grouped-query attention for user prompts of 128K length, and a 3.64x speedup when generating 64K tokens with unlimited streaming. Our code for training on open source data is publicly available at https://github.com/microsoft/Samba.

papers.title: SeRpEnt: Selective Resampling for Expressive State Space Models
papers.abstract: State Space Models (SSMs) have recently enjoyed a rise to prominence in the field of deep learning for sequence modeling, especially as an alternative to Transformers. Their success stems from avoiding two well-known drawbacks of attention-based models: quadratic complexity with respect to the sequence length and inability to model long-range dependencies. The SSM variant Mamba has demonstrated performance comparable to Transformers without any form of attention, thanks to the use of a selective mechanism for the state parameters. Selectivity, however, is only evaluated empirically and the reasons of its effectiveness remain unclear. In this work, we show how selectivity is related to the sequence processing. Our analysis shows that selective time intervals in Mamba act as linear approximators of information. Then, we propose our SeRpEnt architecture, a SSM that further exploits selectivity to compress sequences in an information-aware fashion. It employs a resampling mechanism that aggregates elements based on their information content. Our empirical results in the Long Range Arena benchmark and other language modeling tasks show benefits of the SeRpEnt's resampling mechanism.

papers.title: A Survey on Small Language Models in the Era of Large Language Models: Architecture, Capabilities, and Trustworthiness
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) based on Transformer architecture are powerful but face challenges with deployment, inference latency, and costly fine-tuning. These limitations highlight the emerging potential of small language models (SLMs), which can either replace LLMs through innovative architectures and technologies, or assist them as efficient proxy or reward models. Emerging architectures such as Mamba and xLSTM address the quadratic scaling of inference with window length in Transformers by enabling linear scaling. To maximize SLM performance, test-time compute scaling strategies reduce the performance gap with LLMs by allocating extra compute budget during test time. Beyond standalone usage, SLMs could also assist in LLMs via weak-to-strong learning, proxy tuning, and guarding, fostering secure and efficient LLM deployment. Lastly, the trustworthiness of SLMs remains a critical yet underexplored research area. However, there is a lack of tutorials on cutting-edge SLM technologies, prompting us to conduct one.

papers.title: Multiscale Byte Language Models - A Hierarchical Architecture for Causal Million-Length Sequence Modeling
papers.abstract: Bytes form the basis of the digital world and thus are a promising building block for multimodal foundation models. Recently, Byte Language Models (BLMs) have emerged to overcome tokenization, yet the excessive length of bytestreams requires new architectural paradigms. Therefore, we present the Multiscale Byte Language Model (MBLM), a model-agnostic hierarchical decoder stack that allows training with context windows of $5$M bytes on single GPU in full model precision. We thoroughly examine MBLM's performance with Transformer and Mamba blocks on both unimodal and multimodal tasks. Our experiments demonstrate that hybrid architectures are efficient in handling extremely long byte sequences during training while achieving near-linear generational efficiency. To the best of our knowledge, we present the first evaluation of BLMs on visual Q\&A tasks and find that, despite serializing images and the absence of an encoder, a MBLM with pure next token prediction can match custom CNN-LSTM architectures with designated classification heads. We show that MBLMs exhibit strong adaptability in integrating diverse data representations, including pixel and image filestream bytes, underlining their potential toward omnimodal foundation models. Source code is publicly available at: https://github.com/ai4sd/multiscale-byte-lm

papers.title: CogScale: Scalable Benchmark for Sequence Processing
papers.abstract: The ability to maintain and manipulate information over time is a fundamental aspect of living beings and Artificial Intelligence. While modern models have achieved remarkable success in tasks like natural language processing, evaluating the capacity of novel architectures to process sequential information remains computationally expensive and time-consuming. Testing a new architecture often requires scaling up to massive datasets and models, leading to vast computational costs and slow iteration cycles. In this paper, we propose CogScale, a benchmark of 14 scalable synthetic tasks designed to isolate and evaluate specific cognitive and memory abilities at different parametrizable scales. By providing a standardized, lightweight framework, CogScale allows researchers to rapidly validate architectural innovations before committing to large-scale training. To establish a solid baseline, we evaluate seven distinct architectures: Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), xLSTM, Echo State Network (ESN), Mamba, Transformer Decoder, and Transformer Encoder-Decoder. These evaluations are conducted under strict parameter budgets (1k, 10k, and 100k) and across different difficulty levels and scales. Our results show that while classical RNNs and Echo State Networks excel at basic retention within strict parameter budgets, only attention mechanisms and modern state-space models consistently maintain high performance as reasoning complexity and task difficulty scale.

papers.title: SSMA: A Memory-Efficient Accelerator for State Space Model in the Mamba
papers.abstract: Mamba has exhibited great potential across various tasks, achieving the powerful capability of long-sequence modeling with linear complexity. Selective State Space Models (SSMs), the core component of Mamba, possess unique computational flow and massive memory requirements, which pose new challenges for deployment on edge devices and are difficult to be efficiently supported by existing deep learning accelerators. Therefore, we develop the first memory-efficient Selective SSM Accelerator, namely SSMA. Specifically, we design a reconfigurable hardware architecture and low-complexity nonlinear units to efficiently execute the rearranged and fused operations in Selective SSM. Moreover, we introduce a novel tile-stationary recurrent dataflow to achieve on-chip layer fusion by recurrently updating the tiled latent state and SSM parameters, dramatically decreasing memory usage and access. Experimental results show that the proposed SSMA, evaluated on Xilinx ZCU102 FPGA, achieves up to 3.33× speedup and 41.8 × higher energy efficiency than the optimized GPU implementation with the same setting.

papers.title: Beyond Attention Complexity: A Survey of Efficient and Frugal Transformers for Long-Context Deployment
papers.abstract: Transformer models are now the most common way to model sequences in natural language processing, vision, and multimodal learning. In recent years, their use has quickly moved to long-context situations, where the length of the input has grown from a few thousand tokens to hundreds of thousands or even millions of tokens. This change has completely changed how efficient Transformers are. Early research focused mostly on making self-attention less computationally complex. However, recent large-scale deployments have shown that memory usage during inference, especially due to key-value (KV) caching, is now the main problem for scalability, latency, and energy efficiency. This survey looks at modern Transformer systems from a costand frugality-focused point of view, with a focus on changes that will happen between 2023 and 2025. We first look again at the memory and computational costs of Transformer models during training and inference, focusing on the change from attention computation to memory-bound inference. Next, we look at some recent improvements in efficient attention mechanisms, such as hardware-aware exact attention (like FlashAttention-3) and latent or compressed attention formulations (like Multi-head Latent Attention in DeepSeek-V3) that cut down on KV cache memory by a lot. We also look at new architectural paradigms like state space models (Mamba, Mamba-2) and hybrid attention-SSM architectures, which make it possible to model sequences in linear time and get rid of or reduce KV caching.Lastly, we talk about low-cost training and inference methods, such as low-precision computation, 1-bit large language models, and system-level KV cache optimizations for serving large amounts of data. This survey gives a current look at the design principles that will shape the next generation of efficient and frugal sequence models by bringing together model-level, architectural, and system-level points of view.

ranked_chunks.title: Advancing Intelligent Sequence Modeling: Evolution, Trade-offs, and Applications of State-Space Architectures from S4 to Mamba
ranked_chunks.quote: Structured State Space Models (SSMs) have become a prominent class of sequence models, developed against two long-standing difficulties: the sequential computation and gradient propagation limits of Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), and the quadratic time and memory cost of self-attention in Transformers. By combining structured recurrence with state-space representations, SSMs attain linear or near-linear scaling in sequence length and hold a constant-size recurrent state during autoregressive decoding, so that no key-value cache grows with context. This paper is a structured review of the lineage running from the Structured State Space Sequence model (S4), through its diagonal and simplified successors S4D, Diagonal State Spaces (DSS) and S5, to the selective models Mamba and Mamba-2, and on to SSM-attention hybrids. Rather than describing models one at a time, the analysis is organized around cross-cutting design dimensions: input-dependent selectivity, the recurrent and convolutional views and when each is preferable, diagonalization, cache behavior at inference, hardware-aware kernels, and hybridization. Structured state-space duality is treated as a central thread, because it accounts for the equivalence between the recurrent and the attention-like form and for why hybrid designs work. Reported efficiency and accuracy results are presented with their measurement configuration and evidence level, because observed speedups reflect the combined effects of the algorithm, implementation kernel and hardware rather than an intrinsic property of the model alone. SSMs are competitive with Transformers and more efficient in specific long-context regimes, whereas attention retains an advantage on tasks dominated by exact retrieval and associative recall. The review closes with limitations, failure modes, deployment considerations and open problems.

ranked_chunks.quote: The ability to maintain and manipulate information over time is a fundamental aspect of living beings and Artificial Intelligence. ranked_chunks.title: Beyond Attention Complexity: A Survey of Efficient and Frugal Transformers for Long-Context Deployment
ranked_chunks.quote: Transformer models are now the most common way to model sequences in natural language processing, vision, and multimodal learning. In recent years, their use has quickly moved to long-context situations, where the length of the input has grown from a few thousand tokens to hundreds of thousands or even millions of tokens. This change has completely changed how efficient Transformers are. Early research focused mostly on making self-attention less computationally complex. However, recent large-scale deployments have shown that memory usage during inference, especially due to key-value (KV) caching, is now the main problem for scalability, latency, and energy efficiency. This survey looks at modern Transformer systems from a costand frugality-focused point of view, with a focus on changes that will happen between 2023 and 2025. We first look again at the memory and computational costs of Transformer models during training and inference, focusing on the change from attention computation to memory-bound inference. Next, we look at some recent improvements in efficient attention mechanisms, such as hardware-aware exact attention (like FlashAttention-3) and latent or compressed attention formulations (like Multi-head Latent Attention in DeepSeek-V3) that cut down on KV cache memory by a lot. We also look at new architectural paradigms like state space models (Mamba, Mamba-2) and hybrid attention-SSM architectures, which make it possible to model sequences in linear time and get rid of or reduce KV caching.Lastly, we talk about low-cost training and inference methods, such as low-precision computation, 1-bit large language models, and system-level KV cache optimizations for serving large amounts of data. This survey gives a current look at the design principles that will shape the next generation of efficient and frugal sequence models by bringing together model-level, architectural, and system-level points of view.

ranked_chunks.title: Taipan: Efficient and Expressive State Space Language Models with Selective Attention
ranked_chunks.quote: Efficient long-context language modeling remains a significant challenge in Natural Language Processing (NLP). While Transformers dominate language tasks, they struggle with long sequences due to quadratic computational complexity in training and linearly scaling memory costs during inference. Recent State Space Models (SSMs) such as Mamba offer alternatives with constant memory usage, but they underperform in tasks requiring extensive in-context retrieval. We introduce Taipan, a novel hybrid architecture that combines Mamba-2 with Selective Attention Layers (SALs). These SALs identify tokens requiring long-range interactions, remove less important features, and then augment their representations using the attention module. This approach balances Mamba's efficiency with Transformer-like performance in memory-intensive tasks. ranked_chunks.quote: Efficient long-context language modeling remains a significant challenge in Natural Language Processing (NLP). While Transformers dominate language tasks, they struggle with long sequences due to quadratic computational complexity in training and linearly scaling memory costs during inference. Recent State Space Models (SSMs) such as Mamba offer alternatives with constant memory usage, but they underperform in tasks requiring extensive in-context retrieval. We introduce Taipan, a novel hybrid architecture that combines Mamba-2 with Selective Attention Layers (SALs). These SALs identify tokens requiring long-range interactions, remove less important features, and then augment their representations using the attention module. This approach balances Mamba's efficiency with Transformer-like performance in memory-intensive tasks. By constraining the attention budget, Taipan extends accurate predictions to context lengths of up to 1 million tokens while preserving computational efficiency. Our experiments demonstrate Taipan's superior performance across various scales and tasks, offering a promising solution for efficient long-context language modeling.

ranked_chunks.quote: State-space models (SSMs), particularly the Mamba architecture, have emerged as powerful alternatives to Transformers for sequence modeling, offering linear-time complexity and competitive performance across diverse tasks. However, their large parameter counts pose significant challenges for deployment in resource-constrained environments. We propose a novel unstructured pruning framework tailored for Mamba models that achieves up to 70\% parameter reduction while retaining over 95\% of the original performance. Our approach integrates three key innovations: (1) a gradient-aware magnitude pruning technique that combines weight magnitude and gradient information to identify less critical parameters, (2) an iterative pruning schedule that gradually increases sparsity to maintain model stability, and (3) a global pruning strategy that optimizes parameter allocation across the entire model. Through extensive experiments on WikiText-103, Long Range Arena, and ETT time-series benchmarks, we demonstrate significant efficiency gains with minimal performance degradation. Our analysis of pruning effects on Mamba's components reveals critical insights into the architecture's redundancy and robustness, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained settings while broadening Mamba's applicability.

ranked_chunks.quote: We present Harmonic, a hierarchical state space model (SSM) for language modeling. The architecture stacks three recurrent levels at progressively slower timescales; each level receives the prediction error of the level below as input, rather than its raw hidden state. On enwiki8 with equal token budgets, Harmonic outperforms a comparable Transformer (28M params) by +1.4% at 1K tokens, +6.7% at 8K tokens, and +11.4% at 32K tokens (bpt, lower is better). It also outperforms Mamba at every tested length by 0.7--1.8%. At 64K tokens, both Mamba and Transformer run out of memory on an 80GB H100; Harmonic trains successfully, reaching 6.169 bpt. Results replicate on WikiText-103 (H-TF gap +1.7% to +7.2% across 1K--32K). At 1B parameter scale, replacing all attention layers in TinyLlama 1.1B with HarmonicBlock eliminates the RoPE positional encoding limit: the resulting Hallamonic model maintains stable loss across sequence lengths 1K--8K on two independent clean benchmarks (Lambada and fineweb-edu held-out), while TinyLlama degrades catastrophically past its 2K-token RoPE limit (gap: +9.4 bpt at seq=8K on Lambada). ranked_chunks.title: Samba: Simple Hybrid State Space Models for Efficient Unlimited Context Language Modeling
ranked_chunks.quote: Efficiently modeling sequences with infinite context length has long been a challenging problem. Previous approaches have either suffered from quadratic computational complexity or limited extrapolation ability in length generalization. In this work, we present Samba, a simple hybrid architecture that layer-wise combines Mamba, a selective State Space Model (SSM), with Sliding Window Attention (SWA). Samba selectively compresses a given sequence into recurrent hidden states while still maintaining the ability to precisely recall recent memories with the attention mechanism. We scale Samba up to 3.8B parameters with 3.2T training tokens and demonstrate that it significantly outperforms state-of-the-art models across a variety of benchmarks. Pretrained on sequences of 4K length, Samba shows improved perplexity in context lengths of up to 1M in zero-shot. When finetuned on 4K-length sequences, Samba efficiently extrapolates to a 256K context length with perfect memory recall on the Passkey Retrieval task, and exhibits superior retrieval extrapolation on the challenging Phonebook task compared to full-attention models. As a linear-time sequence model, Samba achieves a 3.73x higher throughput compared to Transformers with grouped-query attention for user prompts of 128K length, and a 3.64x speedup when generating 64K tokens with unlimited streaming. Our code for training on open source data is publicly available at https://github.com/microsoft/Samba.

ranked_chunks.title: SeRpEnt: Selective Resampling for Expressive State Space Models
ranked_chunks.quote: State Space Models (SSMs) have recently enjoyed a rise to prominence in the field of deep learning for sequence modeling, especially as an alternative to Transformers. Their success stems from avoiding two well-known drawbacks of attention-based models: quadratic complexity with respect to the sequence length and inability to model long-range dependencies. The SSM variant Mamba has demonstrated performance comparable to Transformers without any form of attention, thanks to the use of a selective mechanism for the state parameters. Selectivity, however, is only evaluated empirically and the reasons of its effectiveness remain unclear. In this work, we show how selectivity is related to the sequence processing. Our analysis shows that selective time intervals in Mamba act as linear approximators of information. Then, we propose our SeRpEnt architecture, a SSM that further exploits selectivity to compress sequences in an information-aware fashion. It employs a resampling mechanism that aggregates elements based on their information content. Our empirical results in the Long Range Arena benchmark and other language modeling tasks show benefits of the SeRpEnt's resampling mechanism.

ranked_chunks.title: Multiscale Byte Language Models - A Hierarchical Architecture for Causal Million-Length Sequence Modeling
ranked_chunks.quote: Bytes form the basis of the digital world and thus are a promising building block for multimodal foundation models. Recently, Byte Language Models (BLMs) have emerged to overcome tokenization, yet the excessive length of bytestreams requires new architectural paradigms. Therefore, we present the Multiscale Byte Language Model (MBLM), a model-agnostic hierarchical decoder stack that allows training with context windows of $5$M bytes on single GPU in full model precision. We thoroughly examine MBLM's performance with Transformer and Mamba blocks on both unimodal and multimodal tasks. Our experiments demonstrate that hybrid architectures are efficient in handling extremely long byte sequences during training while achieving near-linear generational efficiency. To the best of our knowledge, we present the first evaluation of BLMs on visual Q\&A tasks and find that, despite serializing images and the absence of an encoder, a MBLM with pure next token prediction can match custom CNN-LSTM architectures with designated classification heads. We show that MBLMs exhibit strong adaptability in integrating diverse data representations, including pixel and image filestream bytes, underlining their potential toward omnimodal foundation models. Source code is publicly available at: https://github.com/ai4sd/multiscale-byte-lm

ranked_chunks.title: SSMA: A Memory-Efficient Accelerator for State Space Model in the Mamba
ranked_chunks.quote: Mamba has exhibited great potential across various tasks, achieving the powerful capability of long-sequence modeling with linear complexity. Selective State Space Models (SSMs), the core component of Mamba, possess unique computational flow and massive memory requirements, which pose new challenges for deployment on edge devices and are difficult to be efficiently supported by existing deep learning accelerators. Therefore, we develop the first memory-efficient Selective SSM Accelerator, namely SSMA. Specifically, we design a reconfigurable hardware architecture and low-complexity nonlinear units to efficiently execute the rearranged and fused operations in Selective SSM. Moreover, we introduce a novel tile-stationary recurrent dataflow to achieve on-chip layer fusion by recurrently updating the tiled latent state and SSM parameters, dramatically decreasing memory usage and access. Experimental results show that the proposed SSMA, evaluated on Xilinx ZCU102 FPGA, achieves up to 3.33× speedup and 41.8 × higher energy efficiency than the optimized GPU implementation with the same setting.

ranked_chunks.title: Taipan: Efficient and Expressive State Space Language Models with Selective Attention
ranked_chunks.quote: Efficient long-context language modeling remains a significant challenge in Natural Language Processing (NLP). While Transformers dominate language tasks, they struggle with long sequences due to quadratic computational complexity in training and linearly scaling memory costs during inference. Recent State Space Models (SSMs) such as Mamba offer alternatives with constant memory usage, but they underperform in tasks requiring extensive in-context retrieval. We introduce Taipan, a novel hybrid architecture that combines Mamba-2 with Selective Attention Layers (SALs). These SALs identify tokens requiring long-range interactions, remove less important features, and then augment their representations using the attention module. This approach balances Mamba's efficiency with Transformer-like performance in memory-intensive tasks. By constraining the attention budget, Taipan extends accurate predictions to context lengths of up to 1 million tokens while preserving computational efficiency. Our experiments demonstrate Taipan's superior performance across various scales and tasks, offering a promising solution for efficient long-context language modeling.

ranked_chunks.title: Harmonic: Hierarchical State Space Models for Efficient Long-Context Language Modeling
ranked_chunks.quote: We present Harmonic, a hierarchical state space model (SSM) for language modeling. The architecture stacks three recurrent levels at progressively slower timescales; each level receives the prediction error of the level below as input, rather than its raw hidden state. On enwiki8 with equal token budgets, Harmonic outperforms a comparable Transformer (28M params) by +1.4% at 1K tokens, +6.7% at 8K tokens, and +11.4% at 32K tokens (bpt, lower is better). It also outperforms Mamba at every tested length by 0.7--1.8%. At 64K tokens, both Mamba and Transformer run out of memory on an 80GB H100; Harmonic trains successfully, reaching 6.169 bpt. Results replicate on WikiText-103 (H-TF gap +1.7% to +7.2% across 1K--32K). At 1B parameter scale, replacing all attention layers in TinyLlama 1.1B with HarmonicBlock eliminates the RoPE positional encoding limit: the resulting Hallamonic model maintains stable loss across sequence lengths 1K--8K on two independent clean benchmarks (Lambada and fineweb-edu held-out), while TinyLlama degrades catastrophically past its 2K-token RoPE limit (gap: +9.4 bpt at seq=8K on Lambada). Compute is O(L) per forward pass vs. O(L^2) for attention. Logs: https://github.com/Omibranch/harmonic-logs.

ranked_chunks.title: Samba: Simple Hybrid State Space Models for Efficient Unlimited Context Language Modeling
ranked_chunks.quote: Efficiently modeling sequences with infinite context length has long been a challenging problem. Previous approaches have either suffered from quadratic computational complexity or limited extrapolation ability in length generalization. In this work, we present Samba, a simple hybrid architecture that layer-wise combines Mamba, a selective State Space Model (SSM), with Sliding Window Attention (SWA). Samba selectively compresses a given sequence into recurrent hidden states while still maintaining the ability to precisely recall recent memories with the attention mechanism. We scale Samba up to 3.8B parameters with 3.2T training tokens and demonstrate that it significantly outperforms state-of-the-art models across a variety of benchmarks. Pretrained on sequences of 4K length, Samba shows improved perplexity in context lengths of up to 1M in zero-shot. When finetuned on 4K-length sequences, Samba efficiently extrapolates to a 256K context length with perfect memory recall on the Passkey Retrieval task, and exhibits superior retrieval extrapolation on the challenging Phonebook task compared to full-attention models. As a linear-time sequence model, Samba achieves a 3.73x higher throughput compared to Transformers with grouped-query attention for user prompts of 128K length, and a 3.64x speedup when generating 64K tokens with unlimited streaming. Our code for training on open source data is publicly available at https://github.com/microsoft/Samba.

ranked_chunks.title: SeRpEnt: Selective Resampling for Expressive State Space Models
ranked_chunks.quote: State Space Models (SSMs) have recently enjoyed a rise to prominence in the field of deep learning for sequence modeling, especially as an alternative to Transformers. Their success stems from avoiding two well-known drawbacks of attention-based models: quadratic complexity with respect to the sequence length and inability to model long-range dependencies. The SSM variant Mamba has demonstrated performance comparable to Transformers without any form of attention, thanks to the use of a selective mechanism for the state parameters. Selectivity, however, is only evaluated empirically and the reasons of its effectiveness remain unclear. In this work, we show how selectivity is related to the sequence processing. Our analysis shows that selective time intervals in Mamba act as linear approximators of information. Then, we propose our SeRpEnt architecture, a SSM that further exploits selectivity to compress sequences in an information-aware fashion. It employs a resampling mechanism that aggregates elements based on their information content. Our empirical results in the Long Range Arena benchmark and other language modeling tasks show benefits of the SeRpEnt's resampling mechanism.

ranked_chunks.title: Multiscale Byte Language Models - A Hierarchical Architecture for Causal Million-Length Sequence Modeling
ranked_chunks.quote: Bytes form the basis of the digital world and thus are a promising building block for multimodal foundation models. Recently, Byte Language Models (BLMs) have emerged to overcome tokenization, yet the excessive length of bytestreams requires new architectural paradigms. Therefore, we present the Multiscale Byte Language Model (MBLM), a model-agnostic hierarchical decoder stack that allows training with context windows of $5$M bytes on single GPU in full model precision. We thoroughly examine MBLM's performance with Transformer and Mamba blocks on both unimodal and multimodal tasks. Our experiments demonstrate that hybrid architectures are efficient in handling extremely long byte sequences during training while achieving near-linear generational efficiency. To the best of our knowledge, we present the first evaluation of BLMs on visual Q\&A tasks and find that, despite serializing images and the absence of an encoder, a MBLM with pure next token prediction can match custom CNN-LSTM architectures with designated classification heads. We show that MBLMs exhibit strong adaptability in integrating diverse data representations, including pixel and image filestream bytes, underlining their potential toward omnimodal foundation models. Source code is publicly available at: https://github.com/ai4sd/multiscale-byte-lm

ranked_chunks.title: SSMA: A Memory-Efficient Accelerator for State Space Model in the Mamba
ranked_chunks.quote: Mamba has exhibited great potential across various tasks, achieving the powerful capability of long-sequence modeling with linear complexity. Selective State Space Models (SSMs), the core component of Mamba, possess unique computational flow and massive memory requirements, which pose new challenges for deployment on edge devices and are difficult to be efficiently supported by existing deep learning accelerators. Therefore, we develop the first memory-efficient Selective SSM Accelerator, namely SSMA. Specifically, we design a reconfigurable hardware architecture and low-complexity nonlinear units to efficiently execute the rearranged and fused operations in Selective SSM. Moreover, we introduce a novel tile-stationary recurrent dataflow to achieve on-chip layer fusion by recurrently updating the tiled latent state and SSM parameters, dramatically decreasing memory usage and access. Experimental results show that the proposed SSMA, evaluated on Xilinx ZCU102 FPGA, achieves up to 3.33× speedup and 41.8 × higher energy efficiency than the optimized GPU implementation with the same setting.

ranked_chunks.title: Taipan: Efficient and Expressive State Space Language Models with Selective Attention
ranked_chunks.quote: Efficient long-context language modeling remains a significant challenge in Natural Language Processing (NLP). While Transformers dominate language tasks, they struggle with long sequences due to quadratic computational complexity in training and linearly scaling memory costs during inference. Recent State Space Models (SSMs) such as Mamba offer alternatives with constant memory usage, but they underperform in tasks requiring extensive in-context retrieval. We introduce Taipan, a novel hybrid architecture that combines Mamba-2 with Selective Attention Layers (SALs). These SALs identify tokens requiring long-range interactions, remove less important features, and then augment their representations using the attention module. This approach balances Mamba's efficiency with Transformer-like performance in memory-intensive tasks. By constraining the attention budget, Taipan extends accurate predictions to context lengths of up to 1 million tokens while preserving computational efficiency. Our experiments demonstrate Taipan's superior performance across various scales and tasks, offering a promising solution for efficient long-context language modeling.

ranked_chunks.title: Efficient Unstructured Pruning of Mamba State-Space Models for Resource-Constrained Environments
ranked_chunks.quote: State-space models (SSMs), particularly the Mamba architecture, have emerged as powerful alternatives to Transformers for sequence modeling, offering linear-time complexity and competitive performance across diverse tasks. However, their large parameter counts pose significant challenges for deployment in resource-constrained environments. We propose a novel unstructured pruning framework tailored for Mamba models that achieves up to 70\% parameter reduction while retaining over 95\% of the original performance. Our approach integrates three key innovations: (1) a gradient-aware magnitude pruning technique that combines weight magnitude and gradient information to identify less critical parameters, (2) an iterative pruning schedule that gradually increases sparsity to maintain model stability, and (3) a global pruning strategy that optimizes parameter allocation across the entire model. Through extensive experiments on WikiText-103, Long Range Arena, and ETT time-series benchmarks, we demonstrate significant efficiency gains with minimal performance degradation. Our analysis of pruning effects on Mamba's components reveals critical insights into the architecture's redundancy and robustness, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained settings while broadening Mamba's applicability.

ranked_chunks.title: Harmonic: Hierarchical State Space Models for Efficient Long-Context Language Modeling
ranked_chunks.quote: We present Harmonic, a hierarchical state space model (SSM) for language modeling. The architecture stacks three recurrent levels at progressively slower timescales; each level receives the prediction error of the level below as input, rather than its raw hidden state. On enwiki8 with equal token budgets, Harmonic outperforms a comparable Transformer (28M params) by +1.4% at 1K tokens, +6.7% at 8K tokens, and +11.4% at 32K tokens (bpt, lower is better). It also outperforms Mamba at every tested length by 0.7--1.8%. At 64K tokens, both Mamba and Transformer run out of memory on an 80GB H100; Harmonic trains successfully, reaching 6.169 bpt. Results replicate on WikiText-103 (H-TF gap +1.7% to +7.2% across 1K--32K). At 1B parameter scale, replacing all attention layers in TinyLlama 1.1B with HarmonicBlock eliminates the RoPE positional encoding limit: the resulting Hallamonic model maintains stable loss across sequence lengths 1K--8K on two independent clean benchmarks (Lambada and fineweb-edu held-out), while TinyLlama degrades catastrophically past its 2K-token RoPE limit (gap: +9.4 bpt at seq=8K on Lambada). Compute is O(L) per forward pass vs. O(L^2) for attention. Logs: https://github.com/Omibranch/harmonic-logs.

Abstract:

State Space Models (SSMs) have become serious contenders in the field of sequential modeling, challenging the dominance of Transformers. At the same time, Mixture of Experts (MoE) has significantly improved Transformer-based Large Language Models, including recent state-of-the-art open models. We propose that to unlock the potential of SSMs for scaling, they should be combined with MoE. We showcase this on Mamba, a recent SSM-based model that achieves remarkable performance. Our model, MoE-Mamba, outperforms both Mamba and baseline Transformer-MoE. In particular, MoE-Mamba reaches the same performance as Mamba in $2.35\times$ fewer training steps while preserving the inference performance gains of Mamba against Transformer.

ranked_chunks.title: Taipan: Efficient and Expressive State Space Language Models with Selective Attention
ranked_chunks.quote: Efficient long-context language modeling remains a significant challenge in Natural Language Processing (NLP). While Transformers dominate language tasks, they struggle with long sequences due to quadratic computational complexity in training and linearly scaling memory costs during inference. Recent State Space Models (SSMs) such as Mamba offer alternatives with constant memory usage, but they underperform in tasks requiring extensive in-context retrieval. We introduce Taipan, a novel hybrid architecture that combines Mamba-2 with Selective Attention Layers (SALs). These SALs identify tokens requiring long-range interactions, remove less important features, and then augment their representations using the attention module. This approach balances Mamba's efficiency with Transformer-like performance in memory-intensive tasks. By constraining the attention budget, Taipan extends accurate predictions to context lengths of up to 1 million tokens while preserving computational efficiency. Our experiments demonstrate Taipan's superior performance across various scales and tasks, offering a promising solution for efficient long-context language modeling.

ranked_chunks.title: Efficient Unstructured Pruning of Mamba State-Space Models for Resource-Constrained Environments
ranked_chunks.quote: State-space models (SSMs), particularly the Mamba architecture, have emerged as powerful alternatives to Transformers for sequence modeling, offering linear-time complexity and competitive performance across diverse tasks. However, their large parameter counts pose significant challenges for deployment in resource-constrained environments. We propose a novel unstructured pruning framework tailored for Mamba models that achieves up to 70\% parameter reduction while retaining over 95\% of the original performance. Our approach integrates three key innovations: (1) a gradient-aware magnitude pruning technique that combines weight magnitude and gradient information to identify less critical parameters, (2) an iterative pruning schedule that gradually increases sparsity to maintain model stability, and (3) a global pruning strategy that optimizes parameter allocation across the entire model. Through extensive experiments on WikiText-103, Long Range Arena, and ETT time-series benchmarks, we demonstrate significant efficiency gains with minimal performance degradation. Our analysis of pruning effects on Mamba's components reveals critical insights into the architecture's redundancy and robustness, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained settings while broadening Mamba's applicability.

ranked_chunks.title: Harmonic: Hierarchical State Space Models for Efficient Long-Context Language Modeling
ranked_chunks.quote: We present Harmonic, a hierarchical state space model (SSM) for language modeling. The architecture stacks three recurrent levels at progressively slower timescales; each level receives the prediction error of the level below as input, rather than its raw hidden state. On enwiki8 with equal token budgets, Harmonic outperforms a comparable Transformer (28M params) by +1.4% at 1K tokens, +6.7% at 8K tokens, and +11.4% at 32K tokens (bpt, lower is better). It also outperforms Mamba at every tested length by 0.7--1.8%. At 64K tokens, both Mamba and Transformer run out of memory on an 80GB H100; Harmonic trains successfully, reaching 6.169 bpt. Results replicate on WikiText-103 (H-TF gap +1.7% to +7.2% across 1K--32K). At 1B parameter scale, replacing all attention layers in TinyLlama 1.1B with HarmonicBlock eliminates the RoPE positional encoding limit: the resulting Hallamonic model maintains stable loss across sequence lengths 1K--8K on two independent clean benchmarks (Lambada and fineweb-edu held-out), while TinyLlama degrades catastrophically past its 2K-token RoPE limit (gap: +9.4 bpt at seq=8K on Lambada). ranked_chunks.title: Advancing Intelligent Sequence Modeling: Evolution, Trade-offs, and Applications of State-Space Architectures from S4 to Mamba
ranked_chunks.quote: Structured State Space Models (SSMs) have become a prominent class of sequence models, developed against two long-standing difficulties: the sequential computation and gradient propagation limits of Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), and the quadratic time and memory cost of self-attention in Transformers. By combining structured recurrence with state-space representations, SSMs attain linear or near-linear scaling in sequence length and hold a constant-size recurrent state during autoregressive decoding, so that no key-value cache grows with context. This paper is a structured review of the lineage running from the Structured State Space Sequence model (S4), through its diagonal and simplified successors S4D, Diagonal State Spaces (DSS) and S5, to the selective models Mamba and Mamba-2, and on to SSM-attention hybrids. Rather than describing models one at a time, the analysis is organized around cross-cutting design dimensions: input-dependent selectivity, the recurrent and convolutional views and when each is preferable, diagonalization, cache behavior at inference, hardware-aware kernels, and hybridization. Structured state-space duality is treated as a central thread, because it accounts for the equivalence between the recurrent and the attention-like form and for why hybrid designs work. Reported efficiency and accuracy results are presented with their measurement configuration and evidence level, because observed speedups reflect the combined effects of the algorithm, implementation kernel and hardware rather than an intrinsic property of the model alone. SSMs are competitive with Transformers and more efficient in specific long-context regimes, whereas attention retains an advantage on tasks dominated by exact retrieval and associative recall. The review closes with limitations, failure modes, deployment considerations and open problems.

ranked_chunks.title: Samba: Simple Hybrid State Space Models for Efficient Unlimited Context Language Modeling
ranked_chunks.quote: Efficiently modeling sequences with infinite context length has long been a challenging problem. Previous approaches have either suffered from quadratic computational complexity or limited extrapolation ability in length generalization. In this work, we present Samba, a simple hybrid architecture that layer-wise combines Mamba, a selective State Space Model (SSM), with Sliding Window Attention (SWA). Samba selectively compresses a given sequence into recurrent hidden states while still maintaining the ability to precisely recall recent memories with the attention mechanism. We scale Samba up to 3.8B parameters with 3.2T training tokens and demonstrate that it significantly outperforms state-of-the-art models across a variety of benchmarks. Pretrained on sequences of 4K length, Samba shows improved perplexity in context lengths of up to 1M in zero-shot. When finetuned on 4K-length sequences, Samba efficiently extrapolates to a 256K context length with perfect memory recall on the Passkey Retrieval task, and exhibits superior retrieval extrapolation on the challenging Phonebook task compared to full-attention models. As a linear-time sequence model, Samba achieves a 3.73x higher throughput compared to Transformers with grouped-query attention for user prompts of 128K length, and a 3.64x speedup when generating 64K tokens with unlimited streaming. Our code for training on open source data is publicly available at https://github.com/microsoft/Samba.

ranked_chunks.title: SeRpEnt: Selective Resampling for Expressive State Space Models
ranked_chunks.quote: State Space Models (SSMs) have recently enjoyed a rise to prominence in the field of deep learning for sequence modeling, especially as an alternative to Transformers. Their success stems from avoiding two well-known drawbacks of attention-based models: quadratic complexity with respect to the sequence length and inability to model long-range dependencies. The SSM variant Mamba has demonstrated performance comparable to Transformers without any form of attention, thanks to the use of a selective mechanism for the state parameters. Selectivity, however, is only evaluated empirically and the reasons of its effectiveness remain unclear. In this work, we show how selectivity is related to the sequence processing. Our analysis shows that selective time intervals in Mamba act as linear approximators of information. Then, we propose our SeRpEnt architecture, a SSM that further exploits selectivity to compress sequences in an information-aware fashion. It employs a resampling mechanism that aggregates elements based on their information content. Our empirical results in the Long Range Arena benchmark and other language modeling tasks show benefits of the SeRpEnt's resampling mechanism.

ranked_chunks.title: A Survey on Small Language Models in the Era of Large Language Models: Architecture, Capabilities, and Trustworthiness
ranked_chunks.quote: Large language models (LLMs) based on Transformer architecture are powerful but face challenges with deployment, inference latency, and costly fine-tuning. These limitations highlight the emerging potential of small language models (SLMs), which can either replace LLMs through innovative architectures and technologies, or assist them as efficient proxy or reward models. Emerging architectures such as Mamba and xLSTM address the quadratic scaling of inference with window length in Transformers by enabling linear scaling. To maximize SLM performance, test-time compute scaling strategies reduce the performance gap with LLMs by allocating extra compute budget during test time. Beyond standalone usage, SLMs could also assist in LLMs via weak-to-strong learning, proxy tuning, and guarding, fostering secure and efficient LLM deployment. Lastly, the trustworthiness of SLMs remains a critical yet underexplored research area. However, there is a lack of tutorials on cutting-edge SLM technologies, prompting us to conduct one.

ranked_chunks.title: Multiscale Byte Language Models - A Hierarchical Architecture for Causal Million-Length Sequence Modeling
ranked_chunks.quote: Bytes form the basis of the digital world and thus are a promising building block for multimodal foundation models. Recently, Byte Language Models (BLMs) have emerged to overcome tokenization, yet the excessive length of bytestreams requires new architectural paradigms. Therefore, we present the Multiscale Byte Language Model (MBLM), a model-agnostic hierarchical decoder stack that allows training with context windows of $5$M bytes on single GPU in full model precision. We thoroughly examine MBLM's performance with Transformer and Mamba blocks on both unimodal and multimodal tasks. Our experiments demonstrate that hybrid architectures are efficient in handling extremely long byte sequences during training while achieving near-linear generational efficiency. ranked_chunks.title: CogScale: Scalable Benchmark for Sequence Processing
ranked_chunks.quote: The ability to maintain and manipulate information over time is a fundamental aspect of living beings and Artificial Intelligence. While modern models have achieved remarkable success in tasks like natural language processing, evaluating the capacity of novel architectures to process sequential information remains computationally expensive and time-consuming. Testing a new architecture often requires scaling up to massive datasets and models, leading to vast computational costs and slow iteration cycles. In this paper, we propose CogScale, a benchmark of 14 scalable synthetic tasks designed to isolate and evaluate specific cognitive and memory abilities at different parametrizable scales. By providing a standardized, lightweight framework, CogScale allows researchers to rapidly validate architectural innovations before committing to large-scale training. To establish a solid baseline, we evaluate seven distinct architectures: Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), xLSTM, Echo State Network (ESN), Mamba, Transformer Decoder, and Transformer Encoder-Decoder. These evaluations are conducted under strict parameter budgets (1k, 10k, and 100k) and across different difficulty levels and scales. Our results show that while classical RNNs and Echo State Networks excel at basic retention within strict parameter budgets, only attention mechanisms and modern state-space models consistently maintain high performance as reasoning complexity and task difficulty scale.

ranked_chunks.title: SSMA: A Memory-Efficient Accelerator for State Space Model in the Mamba
ranked_chunks.quote: Mamba has exhibited great potential across various tasks, achieving the powerful capability of long-sequence modeling with linear complexity. Selective State Space Models (SSMs), the core component of Mamba, possess unique computational flow and massive memory requirements, which pose new challenges for deployment on edge devices and are difficult to be efficiently supported by existing deep learning accelerators. Therefore, we develop the first memory-efficient Selective SSM Accelerator, namely SSMA. Specifically, we design a reconfigurable hardware architecture and low-complexity nonlinear units to efficiently execute the rearranged and fused operations in Selective SSM. Moreover, we introduce a novel tile-stationary recurrent dataflow to achieve on-chip layer fusion by recurrently updating the tiled latent state and SSM parameters, dramatically decreasing memory usage and access. Experimental results show that the proposed SSMA, evaluated on Xilinx ZCU102 FPGA, achieves up to 3.33× speedup and 41.8 × higher energy efficiency than the optimized GPU implementation with the same setting.

ranked_chunks.title: Beyond Attention Complexity: A Survey of Efficient and Frugal Transformers for Long-Context Deployment
ranked_chunks.quote: Transformer models are now the most common way to model sequences in natural language processing, vision, and multimodal learning. In recent years, their use has quickly moved to long-context situations, where the length of the input has grown from a few thousand tokens to hundreds of thousands or even millions of tokens. This change has completely changed how efficient Transformers are. Early research focused mostly on making self-attention less computationally complex. However, recent large-scale deployments have shown that memory usage during inference, especially due to key-value (KV) caching, is now the main problem for scalability, latency, and energy efficiency. This survey looks at modern Transformer systems from a costand frugality-focused point of view, with a focus on changes that will happen between 2023 and 2025. We first look again at the memory and computational costs of Transformer models during training and inference, focusing on the change from attention computation to memory-bound inference. Next, we look at some recent improvements in efficient attention mechanisms, such as hardware-aware exact attention (like FlashAttention-3) and latent or compressed attention formulations (like Multi-head Latent Attention in DeepSeek-V3) that cut down on KV cache memory by a lot. We also look at new architectural paradigms like state space models (Mamba, Mamba-2) and hybrid attention-SSM architectures, which make it possible to model sequences in linear time and get rid of or reduce KV caching.Lastly, we talk about low-cost training and inference methods, such as low-precision computation, 1-bit large language models, and system-level KV cache optimizations for serving large amounts of data. This survey gives a current look at the design principles that will shape the next generation of efficient and frugal sequence models by bringing together model-level, architectural, and system-level points of view.

ranked_chunks.quote: The ability to maintain and manipulate information over time is a fundamental aspect of living beings and Artificial Intelligence. While modern models have achieved remarkable success in tasks like natural language processing, evaluating the capacity of novel architectures to process sequential information remains computationally expensive and time-consuming. By providing a standardized, lightweight framework, CogScale allows researchers to rapidly validate architectural innovations before committing to large-scale training. To establish a solid baseline, we evaluate seven distinct architectures: Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), xLSTM, Echo State Network (ESN), Mamba, Transformer Decoder, and Transformer Encoder-Decoder. These evaluations are conducted under strict parameter budgets (1k, 10k, and 100k) and across different difficulty levels and scales. Our results show that while classical RNNs and Echo State Networks excel at basic retention within strict parameter budgets, only attention mechanisms and modern state-space models consistently maintain high performance as reasoning complexity and task difficulty scale.

ranked_chunks.title: Samba: Simple Hybrid State Space Models for Efficient Unlimited Context Language Modeling
ranked_chunks.quote: Efficiently modeling sequences with infinite context length has long been a challenging problem. Previous approaches have either suffered from quadratic computational complexity or limited extrapolation ability in length generalization. In this work, we present Samba, a simple hybrid architecture that layer-wise combines Mamba, a selective State Space Model (SSM), with Sliding Window Attention (SWA). Samba selectively compresses a given sequence into recurrent hidden states while still maintaining the ability to precisely recall recent memories with the attention mechanism. We scale Samba up to 3.8B parameters with 3.2T training tokens and demonstrate that it significantly outperforms state-of-the-art models across a variety of benchmarks. Pretrained on sequences of 4K length, Samba shows improved perplexity in context lengths of up to 1M in zero-shot. When finetuned on 4K-length sequences, Samba efficiently extrapolates to a 256K context length with perfect memory recall on the Passkey Retrieval task, and exhibits superior retrieval extrapolation on the challenging Phonebook task compared to full-attention models. As a linear-time sequence model, Samba achieves a 3.73x higher throughput compared to Transformers with grouped-query attention for user prompts of 128K length, and a 3.64x speedup when generating 64K tokens with unlimited streaming. Our code for training on open source data is publicly available at https://github.com/microsoft/Samba.

These approaches include specialized accelerators like SSMA, which utilizes a tile-stationary recurrent dataflow to achieve on-chip layer fusion, and unstructured pruning techniques that reduce parameter counts. These methods significantly enhance throughput and energy efficiency, with SSMA demonstrating up to 3.33x speedup and 41.8x higher energy efficiency compared to optimized GPU implementations.

ranked_chunks.title: SSMA: A Memory-Efficient Accelerator for State Space Model in the Mamba
ranked_chunks.quote: Mamba has exhibited great potential across various tasks, achieving the powerful capability of long-sequence modeling with linear complexity. Selective State Space Models (SSMs), the core component of Mamba, possess unique computational flow and massive memory requirements, which pose new challenges for deployment on edge devices and are difficult to be efficiently supported by existing deep learning accelerators. Therefore, we develop the first memory-efficient Selective SSM Accelerator, namely SSMA. Specifically, we design a reconfigurable hardware architecture and low-complexity nonlinear units to efficiently execute the rearranged and fused operations in Selective SSM. Moreover, we introduce a novel tile-stationary recurrent dataflow to achieve on-chip layer fusion by recurrently updating the tiled latent state and SSM parameters, dramatically decreasing memory usage and access. Experimental results show that the proposed SSMA, evaluated on Xilinx ZCU102 FPGA, achieves up to 3.33× speedup and 41.8 × higher energy efficiency than the optimized GPU implementation with the same setting.

ranked_chunks.quote: State-space models (SSMs), particularly the Mamba architecture, have emerged as powerful alternatives to Transformers for sequence modeling, offering linear-time complexity and competitive performance across diverse tasks. However, their large parameter counts pose significant challenges for deployment in resource-constrained environments. We propose a novel unstructured pruning framework tailored for Mamba models that achieves up to 70\% parameter reduction while retaining over 95\% of the original performance. Our approach integrates three key innovations: (1) a gradient-aware magnitude pruning technique that combines weight magnitude and gradient information to identify less critical parameters, (2) an iterative pruning schedule that gradually increases sparsity to maintain model stability, and (3) a global pruning strategy that optimizes parameter allocation across the entire model. Through extensive experiments on WikiText-103, Long Range Arena, and ETT time-series benchmarks, we demonstrate significant efficiency gains with minimal performance degradation. Our analysis of pruning effects on Mamba's components reveals critical insights into the architecture's redundancy and robustness, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained settings while broadening Mamba's applicability.

Then, we propose our SeRpEnt architecture, a SSM that further exploits selectivity to compress sequences in an information-aware fashion. It employs a resampling mechanism that aggregates elements based on their information content. Our empirical results in the Long Range Arena benchmark and other language modeling tasks show benefits of the SeRpEnt's resampling mechanism.

literature_review.title: Advancements in Mamba Architectures for Long-Context Language Modeling
literature_review.abstract: The emergence of state space models (SSMs), particularly the Mamba architecture, has provided a compelling alternative to traditional Transformer-based models for long-context language modeling. Recent research has focused on addressing the inherent limitations of these architectures, specifically regarding scaling, representation bottlenecks, and sequence modeling efficiency. This review synthesizes recent methodological advancements, including the integration of Mixture of Experts (MoE), the implementation of motif-constrained pathways, and the development of hierarchical memory mechanisms. These innovations demonstrate significant improvements in training efficiency, retrieval performance, and reasoning capabilities while maintaining the computational advantages of linear-time sequence modeling.
literature_review.introduction: State space models have gained prominence as a robust framework for processing long sequences, offering a departure from the quadratic complexity associated with standard attention mechanisms. The Mamba architecture, a selective state space model, has established a new benchmark for performance in this domain. However, as the demand for longer context windows and more complex reasoning tasks grows, researchers have sought to refine the Mamba architecture to overcome specific structural constraints. Current efforts are directed toward enhancing the scalability of these models, addressing the fixed-capacity limitations of recurrent states, and embedding domain-specific structural information into the modeling process. This report examines three primary architectural interventions: the integration of Mixture of Experts, the use of motif-constrained pathways, and the introduction of hierarchical memory systems.

sections.title: Scaling Mamba via Mixture of Experts
paragraphs: A primary challenge in scaling state space models is ensuring that performance gains remain consistent as model size increases. To address this, researchers have proposed the integration of Mixture of Experts (MoE) with the Mamba architecture. The rationale behind this approach is that combining the selective state space model with MoE can unlock greater potential for scaling [[W4390723179]].

The MoE-Mamba architecture demonstrates that this hybrid approach is highly effective. By incorporating MoE, the model achieves the same performance as the standard Mamba model while requiring 2.35x fewer training steps [[W4390723179]]. Furthermore, this architecture successfully preserves the inference performance gains that Mamba provides when compared to traditional Transformer models [[W4390723179]]. This suggests that the modularity offered by MoE is a viable strategy for improving the training efficiency of state space models without sacrificing their inherent architectural advantages.

sections.title: Motif-Constrained State Space Modeling
paragraphs: Beyond scaling, there is a need to improve the efficiency of long-sequence modeling by incorporating structural priors. The Motif-Mamba architecture introduces a motif-constrained state space model designed to enhance Mamba for long-sequence tasks [[arxiv:2608.00027v1]]. The core innovation of this approach is the design of a low-rank recurrent pathway that embeds motif-guided state interactions into the Mamba framework [[arxiv:2608.00027v1]].

This design choice is significant because it allows the model to leverage specific structural motifs while simultaneously preserving the linear-time sequence modeling capabilities that define the Mamba architecture [[arxiv:2608.00027v1]]. By embedding these interactions directly into the state space, Motif-Mamba provides a mechanism for more nuanced sequence processing, which is essential for tasks where long-range dependencies are governed by underlying structural patterns.

sections.title: Hierarchical Memory Mechanisms
paragraphs: A persistent limitation in recurrent state models is the representation bottleneck caused by fixed-capacity recurrent states. To overcome this, the Hierarchical Memory Mamba (HMM) has been proposed, drawing inspiration from hierarchical human memory systems [[arxiv:2608.02347v2]]. The HMM architecture integrates two distinct memory components: a parametric working memory for semantic encoding and retrieval, and a non-parametric long-term memory (LTM) storage [[arxiv:2608.02347v2]].

This dual-memory approach effectively circumvents the bottleneck imposed by fixed recurrent states, allowing for more flexible information management [[arxiv:2608.02347v2]]. The empirical results for HMM are notable: compared to existing Mamba-based variants, HMM achieves significant gains in both retrieval and reasoning performance [[arxiv:2608.02347v2]]. Crucially, these improvements are achieved with minimal training overhead and by introducing only 2% additional parameters, demonstrating the efficiency of the hierarchical memory design in enhancing the capabilities of Mamba-based systems [[arxiv:2608.02347v2]].

literature_review.conclusion: The evolution of Mamba-based architectures reflects a concerted effort to enhance the efficiency and capability of state space models for long-context language modeling. The integration of Mixture of Experts has proven effective in reducing training requirements, while motif-constrained pathways and hierarchical memory mechanisms have addressed structural and capacity-related bottlenecks. These advancements collectively demonstrate that the Mamba architecture is highly adaptable, allowing for specialized modifications that significantly improve performance in retrieval and reasoning tasks while maintaining the computational efficiency required for long-sequence processing.
literature_review.limitations: This review is constrained by the scope of the provided evidence. The synthesis is limited to the specific architectural interventions identified in the source material, namely MoE-Mamba, Motif-Mamba, and Hierarchical Memory Mamba. No broader analysis of the entire landscape of state space models or their comparative performance against all existing Transformer variants is provided. Furthermore, the quantitative results cited are specific to the reported experiments within the provided papers and should be interpreted within the context of those specific benchmarks and methodologies.
